# Introduction

At a heterozygous SNP, both alleles are in the same nucleus and in the same ATAC-seq library. If one allele gets more reads than the other, the variant itself changes accessibility. This is allele-specific chromatin accessibility (ASC).

`ChrAccR` stores allele counts in a `DsASC` object. It holds two matrices, reference reads and alternative reads, with one row per SNP and one column per sample.

This vignette has two parts:

1. **Quick start.** The analysis on a small example dataset. Every chunk runs.
2. **Your own data.** How to build a `DsASC` object from BAM and VCF files. These chunks are shown but not run, because they need the full dataset.

The example comes from the immune cell atlas of [@Calderon:2019cb]. The complete re-analysis is in the [AlleleSpeC repository](https://github.com/EpigenomeInformatics/allele_spec).

# Installation

The ASC functions are in the `alleleSpec` branch of `ChrAccR`. The example data are in `ChrAccRex`.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
if (!is.element('devtools', installed.packages()[,"Package"])) install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github("EpigenomeInformatics/ChrAccR", ref = "alleleSpec", dependencies = TRUE)
devtools::install_github("EpigenomeInformatics/ChrAccRex")

# needed for counting, for the sharing estimate and for the motif analysis
BiocManager::install(c("VariantAnnotation", "Rsamtools", "HDF5Array", "DelayedArray",
                       "JASPAR2020", "TFBSTools", "motifmatchr",
                       "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38"))
install.packages("ashr")
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(ChrAccR)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
```

# The workflow at a glance

![The ASC workflow in `ChrAccR`. The last box includes the optional filter for sites that are supported by at least two donors.](figures/asc_workflow.png)

| Step | What happens | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Genotype each donor | GATK (outside R) |
| 2 | Remove mapping bias | WASP (outside R) |
| 3 | Build one SNP list for all donors | `buildMasterSNPs()` |
| 4 | Count reference and alternative reads | `DsASC.gatk()` |
| 5 | Keep SNPs in peaks | `annotateASCSites()`, `filterASCByPeaks()` |
| 6 | Remove likely errors | `ascDropHomozygous()`, `ascFilterRegions()`, `ascFilterCommonVariants()` |
| 7 | Sum technical replicates | `ascPoolReplicates()` |
| 8 | Test each site | `ascTestCounts()`, `calcASCStatistics()` |
| 9 | Optional: keep sites found in several donors | `filterForRecurrence()` |
| 10 | Compare conditions or cell types | `ascAggregate()`, `ascSharing()` |
| 11 | Link imbalance to TF motifs | `ascMotifPreference()`, `ascPreferenceTable()`, `ascPreferenceTest()` |

Steps 1 and 2 run outside R. Every step after WASP is a `ChrAccR` function.

# Quick start with the example data

## Load the example

The example holds one donor (1001) with resting and stimulated samples. Steps 1 to 7 of the workflow are already done. It also contains precomputed motif scores.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
example   <- ChrAccRex::loadExample("dsAsc_ia_example")
dsDemo    <- example$ds
deltaDemo <- example$delta
annotDemo <- as.data.table(getSampleAnnot(dsDemo))
dsDemo
```

## Look at the counts

`getRefCounts()` and `getAltCounts()` return the two count matrices. `getAllelicBalance()` returns the fraction of reads on the alternative allele, and sets sites below `minCoverage` to `NA`.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
refMat <- as.matrix(getRefCounts(dsDemo))
altMat <- as.matrix(getAltCounts(dsDemo))
dim(refMat)

balance <- getAllelicBalance(dsDemo, minCoverage = 10)
summary(as.vector(balance))
```

The median should be close to 0.5. Most heterozygous sites are balanced, and ASC sites are the exceptions.

## Test each site

`calcASCStatistics()` runs a two-sided binomial test against 0.5 for every site in every sample. P-values are corrected with the Benjamini-Hochberg method within each sample.

Two thresholds decide which sites are tested:

* `minCoverage`: the number of reads a site needs in total.
* `minAllele`: the number of reads each allele needs. This removes sites where only one allele was seen, which are often genotyping errors.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
ascStats <- calcASCStatistics(dsDemo, minCoverage = 10, minAllele = 2)
ascStats[order(fdr)][1:5, .(snpId, sampleId, ref, alt, total, log2FC, fdr)]
```

A site with an FDR below 0.1 is called ASC. The volcano plot shows effect size against significance. The Manhattan plot shows the same calls along the genome.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
plotASCVolcano(dsDemo, stats = ascStats, sigCut = 0.1)
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
plotASCManhattan(dsDemo, stats = ascStats, sigCut = 0.1)
```

With several donors, you can keep only the sites that are significant in at least two of them. This step is optional.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
recurrent <- filterForRecurrence(ascStats, minDonors = 2, fdrCutoff = 0.1)
```

## Plot one site across cell types

`plotASCBalance()` shows one site in every sample. Each row is a sample, the point is the fraction of reads on the reference allele, and the bar is its 95% confidence interval. Faded points are not significant.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.height = 5}
topSite <- ascStats[order(fdr)][1, snpId]
plotASCBalance(dsDemo, topSite, colorBy = "stimulus", orderBy = "cellType",
               sigStats = ascStats, sigCut = 0.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(S = "#C0392B", U = "#2C7FB8"), name = "stimulus")
```

## Compare resting and stimulated cells

Is a site that is imbalanced in resting cells also imbalanced after stimulation? `ascAggregate()` sums the reads over a set of samples. `ascSharing()` takes the sites that are significant in the first set and sorts them into three groups in the second set:

* **Inaccessible**: fewer than `minReadsB` reads, so the site cannot be judged.
* **Shared**: the imbalance is still there, estimated with `ashr` [@Stephens:2017kb].
* **Not shared**: the site has reads, but no imbalance.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
resting    <- ascAggregate(refMat, altMat, annotDemo[stimulus == "U", sampleId])
stimulated <- ascAggregate(refMat, altMat, annotDemo[stimulus == "S", sampleId])

ascSharing(resting$ref, resting$alt, stimulated$ref, stimulated$alt,
           fdrA = 0.01, minReadsB = 4)
```

The result is the fraction of sites in each group. It is `NULL` if no site is significant in the first set. The same call works for two cell types: pass the samples of each cell type to `ascAggregate()`.

## Link imbalance to TF motifs

If a variant weakens a TF motif, the allele with the weaker motif should be less accessible. `ascMotifPreference()` scores the sequence around each SNP with a motif, once per allele, and gives each SNP a preference:

* **Reference** or **Alternative**: the motif matches this allele better. The score differs by more than `prefDelta`, and a motif match overlaps the SNP.
* **No preference**: all other SNPs.

Here we score two motifs of JASPAR 2020 [@Fornes:2020ja]: JUNB, which is activated by stimulation, and CTCF as a control.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
motifPkgs <- c("JASPAR2020", "TFBSTools", "motifmatchr", "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38")
canScore  <- all(sapply(motifPkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE))
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = canScore}
pwms <- lapply(c(JUNB = "MA0490.2", CTCF = "MA0139.1"), function(id)
  TFBSTools::getMatrixByID(JASPAR2020::JASPAR2020, id))

prefDt <- ascMotifPreference(rownames(refMat), pwms,
                             genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
prefDt[, .N, by = .(tf, preference)]
```

Without the motif packages, the scores that come with the example are used instead.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = !canScore}
prefDt <- copy(deltaDemo)
prefDt[, preference := fifelse(delta >  1, "Alternative",
                       fifelse(delta < -1, "Reference", "No preference"))]
prefDt[, .N, by = .(tf, preference)]
```

`ascPreferenceTable()` adds the reference allele fraction of each SNP in a set of samples. We use resting and stimulated samples of one cell type. SNPs with fewer than four reads are dropped.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# the cell type with the most samples in both conditions
ctCounts <- annotDemo[, .(nU = sum(stimulus == "U"), nS = sum(stimulus == "S")), by = cellType]
focusCt  <- ctCounts[nU > 0 & nS > 0][order(-(nU + nS))][1, cellType]
samplesU <- annotDemo[cellType == focusCt & stimulus == "U", sampleId]
samplesS <- annotDemo[cellType == focusCt & stimulus == "S", sampleId]

prefTab <- rbind(
  ascPreferenceTable(refMat, altMat, samplesU, prefDt, minReads = 4)[, condition := "Resting"],
  ascPreferenceTable(refMat, altMat, samplesS, prefDt, minReads = 4)[, condition := "Stimulated"])
prefTab[, preference := factor(preference, levels = c("Alternative", "No preference", "Reference"))]
```

If the TF opens chromatin, SNPs that prefer the reference allele lie above 0.5 and SNPs that prefer the alternative allele lie below it.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(prefTab, aes(x = condition, y = refFrac, fill = preference)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  facet_wrap(~ tf, ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Alternative"   = "#1B9E77",
                               "No preference" = "#D95F02",
                               "Reference"     = "#7570B3"), name = "Binding preference") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of reads on the reference allele", title = focusCt) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

`ascPreferenceTest()` compares the two groups of each motif with a Wilcoxon test. The table also gives the number of SNPs in each group.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
tests <- prefTab[, ascPreferenceTest(.SD), by = condition]
tests[, pAdj := p.adjust(p, method = "bonferroni")]   # over all motifs and both conditions
tests
```

In the full dataset, the AP-1 family motifs (BATF, FOSL1, JUNB and others) separate weakly in resting cells and strongly after stimulation. Motifs such as CTCF, GATA3, IRF4, NFKB1 and TCF7 do not separate after stimulation.

# Running the analysis on your own data

The chunks in this section are not run.

## What you need

* **BAM files** after mapping-bias correction with WASP [@vandeGeijn:2015hs]. Reads with the alternative allele map slightly worse, which shifts every site towards the reference allele. WASP removes this.
* **One VCF file per donor** with heterozygous SNPs, named `{donor}_heterozygous.vcf.gz`. Without genotyping arrays, the SNPs can be called from the ATAC-seq reads with GATK HaplotypeCaller [@McKenna:2010gk].
* **A sample annotation** with the columns `sampleId`, `bamFilename` and `donor`. Add `cellType` and `stimulus` for the comparisons.
* **A peak set**, for example the consensus peaks of the `DsATAC` object of the same samples.

## Build one SNP list

Each donor is heterozygous at different sites. `buildMasterSNPs()` reads all VCF files and returns one sorted list, so that all objects have the same rows.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
masterGr <- buildMasterSNPs(donors = unique(meta$donor), vcfDir = vcfDir, genome = "hg38")
```

## Count the alleles

`DsASC.gatk()` counts the reference and alternative reads at every SNP. A sample is counted only at the SNPs that are heterozygous in its donor; all other entries are `NA`. With `diskDump = TRUE` the counts are kept on disk, which saves memory.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
dsAsc <- DsASC.gatk(
  sampleAnnot = as.data.frame(meta),
  vcfDir      = vcfDir,
  genome      = "hg38",
  diskDump    = TRUE,
  masterGr    = masterGr
)
```

For a large dataset, run one job per cell type and pass the same `masterGr` to each.

## Keep SNPs in peaks

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
dsAtac <- loadDsAcc(atacDir)
peakGr <- getCoord(dsAtac, "cons_peaks")
names(peakGr) <- paste0("peak_", seq_along(peakGr))

dsAsc <- filterChroms(dsAsc, remove = c("chrX", "chrY", "chrM"))
dsAsc <- filterLowCovg(dsAsc, thresh = 5, reqSamples = 1)   # 5 reads in at least one sample
dsAsc <- annotateASCSites(dsAsc, peakGr)
dsAsc <- filterASCByPeaks(dsAsc)
```

## Remove likely errors

Four steps clean the counts before testing. Each one removes a known source of false calls.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
refMat <- as.matrix(getRefCounts(dsAsc))
altMat <- as.matrix(getAltCounts(dsAsc))
annot  <- as.data.table(getSampleAnnot(dsAsc))

# 1. Genotyping errors: a site that shows only one allele in all reads of a donor
#    is homozygous. Its counts are set to zero for that donor.
cleaned <- ascDropHomozygous(refMat, altMat, annot, minMinor = 2L, minTotal = 10L)

# 2. Regions with poor mappability: remove SNPs in the ENCODE blacklist.
keepIds <- ascFilterRegions(rownames(cleaned$ref), blacklistGr)

# 3. Rare variants: keep SNPs with an allele frequency above 1% in 1000 Genomes.
#    Rare and unknown variants are often homozygous sites that were called heterozygous.
library(MafDb.1Kgenomes.phase3.GRCh38)
keepIds <- ascFilterCommonVariants(keepIds, MafDb.1Kgenomes.phase3.GRCh38, minMaf = 0.01)

# 4. Technical replicates: sum them, so that each test uses one biological sample.
pooled <- ascPoolReplicates(cleaned$ref[keepIds, ], cleaned$alt[keepIds, ], annot,
                            groupCols = c("cellType", "stimulus", "donor"))
```

Step 3 matters most when the genotypes come from the ATAC-seq reads. With genotypes from arrays you can skip it.

## Test each site

`ascTestCounts()` runs the same test as `calcASCStatistics()`, but on the cleaned count matrices.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
ascStats <- ascTestCounts(pooled$ref, pooled$alt, minCoverage = 10, minAllele = 2)
ascStats[fdr < 0.1, .N, by = sampleId]     # ASC sites per sample
```

## Continue as in the quick start

The functions of the quick start take the same count matrices:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# resting against stimulated
resting    <- ascAggregate(pooled$ref, pooled$alt, pooled$annot[stimulus == "U", sampleId])
stimulated <- ascAggregate(pooled$ref, pooled$alt, pooled$annot[stimulus == "S", sampleId])
ascSharing(resting$ref, resting$alt, stimulated$ref, stimulated$alt)

# TF motifs
prefDt  <- ascMotifPreference(rownames(pooled$ref), pwms, genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
prefTab <- ascPreferenceTable(pooled$ref, pooled$alt, pooled$annot[stimulus == "S", sampleId], prefDt)
ascPreferenceTest(prefTab)
```
